sourceBindings.text: A crop group helps you make a shortlist. A recommendation needs evidence about the particular field, season, water supply and crop. Practise with a clearly labelled temperate teaching case, then state what must change before advising an Egyptian farm.
Screen at least two candidate crops from each practical group for the given 10-hectare case, stating a reason, a condition and any missing data for each rather than asserting eight proven matches.

Connect soil texture, drainage, pH, nutrient results, water, temperature, season and light to a reasoned year-one recommendation; keep the case's temperate climate separate from an evidence-based Egyptian locality.
Distinguish annual or seasonal field crops from multi-year plantings and explain why investment duration, drainage and crop-specific pH matter to a plan.

Preserve all negations, conditions, scene-safety restrictions and limits of training. Do not add medical advice, diagnoses, character voices, an introduction, music or an extra summary.

sourceBindings.text: Build a site card with the six exact supplied facts, and separate unprovided drainage, water supply, season, salinity, cultivar and pest evidence. Do not fill unknowns by guesswork.

Enter at least two crops per group with one plausible match, one limiting or missing condition, likely occupancy duration and the data needed to decide. Include the named model alternatives rather than replacing them silently.
Write a year-one crop-group recommendation, one candidate crop, its purpose, the expected benefit and three checks before advising the farmer.

If this teaching case were moved to a named Egyptian locality, list the climate, water, soil and season data you would gather before writing a new recommendation. Keep the original temperate model labelled.
Exact model values stay separate from an Egyptian field observation; every unknown must be marked for verification.

A trainer can supervise reading a local site card or field observation and discuss case assumptions. This step assesses reasoning online; it does not certify an observed physical skill or authorize a crop/fertiliser prescription for a real farm.

sourceBindings.text: crop suitability
A judgement that a specified crop's needs can be met by a specific site and management system, with stated evidence and remaining uncertainty.
sandy loam
A mineral soil texture class with more sand than many loams but enough finer particles to differ from pure sand; it does not alone describe drainage.
soil pH
A measure of acidity or alkalinity; pH 7 is neutral and pH 6.2 is slightly acidic.
drainage
Movement and removal of excess water from the root zone; affected by texture, structure, profile and water outlet.
perennial
A plant whose life cycle can continue for more than two years; actual cropping duration may be shorter if deliberately terminated.
cover crop
A crop grown primarily to cover and manage soil rather than to harvest its main market product; species and management determine its effects.
photoperiod
The duration of daylight, which can affect growth, flowering and maturity depending on crop and variety.
